transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It feels like everything I built after my divorce has collapsed, and I’m just… sitting under all of it.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hopeless feeling?
About a month now. It started around when the financial mess from the divorce really hit, and since then it’s just been hanging over me.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t been paying much attention to what I enjoy lately. It’s more like I just get through the day.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself?
Yes. I’ve been thinking things like it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. It got intense enough that it really scared me, so I called the employee assistance program.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how you're moving compared to before you started feeling this way?

Yes. My energy is really low. Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete, and even basic things like taking a shower or opening my laptop feel like they take more energy than I have.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping?

Yes. I’m not sleeping well at all. Some nights I just lie there staring at the ceiling, going over bills or mistakes I made at work. Other times I wake up before dawn and feel like I never really slept.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite since you started feeling this way?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change in my appetite one way or the other.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual or do you find yourself fidgeting or restless?

I’m more restless, I think. I keep pushing myself into things—extra proposals at work, calling colleagues with ideas, volunteering for tasks no one even asked me to do. And when there’s nothing useful left to do, I’ll just pace around my apartment.
Do you often find yourself thinking that you're to blame for things that have gone wrong?

Yes. I do that a lot. I keep telling myself I’m a terrible engineer, and that I failed as a wife, and that I’m just a burden. I replay every missed calculation or tense email in my head like it proves I ruin things.
Do you feel guilty about things that you've done or haven't done?

Yes. I feel guilty all the time, honestly. I keep thinking I’m a terrible engineer, that I failed as a wife, and that I’m just a burden. Even small things, like a missed calculation or a tense email, I replay them and it feels like proof that I ruin things.
Have you experienced any strange thoughts or heard voices that others couldn't hear since you've been feeling this way?
I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or anything like that. My thoughts can get intense, but not strange in that way.
Do you feel like these feelings of hopelessness and guilt are interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Yes. It’s been affecting everything. At work I was making questionable calls and then falling apart in meetings, and my supervisor had to take me off active project decisions. At home I stopped keeping up with basic routines, and it got bad enough that I ended up being sent to the emergency department because I didn’t feel safe with my thoughts.
Do you feel like these feelings have been constant since they started, or have they been varying in intensity?
It’s been pretty constant. It’s been hanging over me for about a month now, starting around the financial mess after the divorce. Some moments are worse than others, but it hasn’t really lifted.
Have you experienced any episodes where reality seems distorted or you've had beliefs that aren't based in reality since you've been feeling this way?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had beliefs like that or felt like reality was distorted. I’ve just been feeling really overwhelmed, but not disconnected from what’s real.
Do you feel like you're moving or reacting slower than usual, or is it the opposite, where you can't seem to slow down?

It’s more like I can’t slow down. I keep pushing myself into extra proposals, calling colleagues with new ideas, volunteering for tasks no one even asked me to take on. And then at home I’ll pace around my apartment when there’s nothing useful left to do.
Have you had any thoughts or beliefs that you think might not be true, but that you believe anyway, since you've been feeling this way?
Not really. I can’t think of any belief I’m holding onto that I know might not be true. I’ve been stressed and wound up, but I don’t think I’m believing things that don’t make sense.
Have you had any periods where you felt slightly better, even if just for a few days, since this heavy, hopeless feeling started?
No, not really. Since this started, it’s just been this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t shake. It feels like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just sitting under it.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms were so severe that you couldn't get out of bed or perform basic self-care?

Yes. It got to the point where I wasn’t really functioning. At work I was making bad calls and falling apart in meetings, and my supervisor had to take me off active project decisions. At home, I stopped keeping up with basic routines. And… I ended up being sent to the emergency department because I didn’t feel safe with my thoughts.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms improved for at least two weeks since this heavy, hopeless feeling started?

No. I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that. It’s been hanging over me for about a month now, since the financial mess after the divorce, and it hasn’t really lifted for two weeks or anything like that.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms were less severe for a few days, allowing you to feel somewhat better, since this heavy feeling started?
No… I haven’t really had even a few days where it felt lighter. It’s been this same heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I had rebuilt after the divorce just collapsed, and I’m stuck under it.
